texts.facts: 2. The writ petitioner is the appellant herein before this Court. The facts in a nutshell reveal that the father of the appellant, Late Jayabalan, executed two settlement deeds dated 13.01.2014 and 31.12.2014 in favour of the appellant herein, bequeathing some of the properties. Similarly, settlement deeds were executed in favour of the elder son of the deceased senior citizen. The senior citizen filed a complaint before the Revenue Divisional Officer/Tribunal under the provisions of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, seeking cancellation of settlement deed mainly on the ground that the appellant failed to maintain the senior citizen. The Tribunal adjudicated the issues by affording opportunity to the parties. The Senior Citizen deposed before the Tribunal that the appellant/younger son by way of coercion, executed settlement deeds by J.Chakrabani vs The District Collector on 22 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102078987/ 2 promising that he will take care of him during his life time. Since the appellant failed to honour his commitments, senior citizen filed a police complaint. Negotiation meeting was conducted by the Deputy Superintendent of Police in his office, and the appellant promised that he will pay monthly maintenance to the senior citizen. Since the appellant failed to pay maintenance amount as https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/10/2025 07:14:38 pm ) promised by him before the Deputy Superintendent of Police, the Senior Citizen was constrained to file a complaint under the Senior Citizens Act. Since the appellant failed in his duty as mandated under the Senior Citizens Act, the settlement deed in Doc Nos.4548 of 2014 dated 03.12.2014 and 584 of 2014, dated 04.02.2014, executed in favour of the appellant by the senior citizen were cancelled. 3. During his life time, the senior citizen executed two settlement deeds in favour of his grandchildren and subsequently, died on 23.07.2021. The appellant preferred an appeal before the District Collector, since the appeal is not maintenable under the Act, it was rejected. Thus, the writ petition came to be instituted. 4. The Writ Court considered the issues and held that the appellant has to approach the competent Civil Court of law for the purpose of redressing his grievances. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/10/2025 07:14:38 pm )
